subject: Enhanced dissipation for passive scalars
scope: Prescribed incompressible velocities; passive scalar equation and explicitly labeled inviscid, anomalous, generalized-diffusion and stochastic extensions. Non-exhaustive.

records.title: Mixing in incompressible flows: transport, dissipation, and their interplay
records.journal: Notices of the American Mathematical Society 71(5), 593–604
records.topic: survey; mixing; enhanced and anomalous dissipation
records.annotation: Readable survey connecting optimal mixing, transport regularity, enhanced dissipation and anomalous dissipation. A good source for the wiki's introductory architecture and wider bibliography, while detailed theorem statements and proofs should cite the original papers.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation by advection and applications to PDEs
records.topic: survey; hypocoercivity; resolvent; nonlinear applications
records.annotation: Recent survey of enhanced-dissipation mechanisms and methods, including hypocoercivity, resolvent estimates and comparison with Taylor dispersion. Published issue year is 2026, although preprint and DOI string are dated 2025. Use its linear passive-scalar sections as an orientation and bibliography source; nonlinear applications are outside the present collection.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Diffusion and mixing in fluid flow
records.topic: relaxation enhancement; spectral criterion
records.annotation: Foundational characterization of steady relaxation-enhancing incompressible flows on compact manifolds: the transport generator has no nonconstant H1 eigenfunctions. Weak mixing is sufficient, but not necessary. The theorem is qualitative in the large-amplitude limit; it does not by itself supply an explicit small-diffusivity decay rate.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Dissipation enhancement by mixing
records.topic: mixing-to-dissipation; continuous and discrete time
records.annotation: Bounds dissipation time and energy decay using quantitative strong or weak mixing hypotheses, for continuous advection-diffusion and for diffusion interposed with a mixing map. Particularly useful for defining dissipation time and distinguishing discrete/pulsed estimates from continuous-time estimates; the resulting bounds need not be sharp for a specified flow.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: On the relation between enhanced dissipation timescales and mixing rates
records.journal: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 73(6), 1205–1244
records.topic: quantitative mixing-to-dissipation; inviscid-viscous comparison
records.annotation: Converts decay of negative Sobolev mixing norms into enhanced-dissipation bounds using inviscid-viscous comparison, frequency localization and contradiction. Covers abstract models, shear/radial examples, fractional diffusion and contact Anosov flows. Useful for the conceptual proof module; one should state the relevant regularity and mixing hypotheses instead of asserting that mixing alone determines a sharp dissipation time.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Diffusion and mixing in fluid flow via the resolvent estimate
records.topic: resolvent estimates; quantitative Gearhart–Prüss; rough shears
records.annotation: Quantitative semigroup bound for m-accretive operators from a lower bound on the resolvent scale. Applications give a proof of the relaxation-enhancing criterion and logarithmic dissipation times for certain Weierstrass shears. Central reusable tool for a proof chapter. Metadata caution: the arXiv journal-reference field is stale; the established volume citation is 64 (2021), 507–518, with online publication in 2019.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Bounds on the rate of enhanced dissipation
records.topic: limitations on dissipation rate; Sobolev velocity budgets
records.annotation: Bounds the maximal exponential dissipation rate from velocity-gradient integrability using logarithmic-cost transport distances. Under an averaged Sobolev gradient budget, logarithmic restrictions match known optimal constructions. The hypotheses include normalized initial-data regularity and the decay prefactor; an upper bound on an asserted exponential rate is not the same as a lower bound for every scalar at every time.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Exponentially mixing flows with slow enhanced dissipation
records.topic: Mixing versus dissipation; regularity limitations
records.annotation: Constructs a diffusivity-dependent family of smooth incompressible velocities, uniformly bounded in C^0 but not uniformly Lipschitz, with dissipation time of order 1/kappa. The inviscid mixing bound has a kappa-independent exponential rate and prefactor at even integer starting/increment times, with polynomial dependence on the starting time. Its extension to all real times has an additional kappa^(-2) prefactor. This does not establish a single fixed continuous exponentially mixing velocity without enhanced dissipation. Also improves quantitative mixing-to-dissipation bounds, including dependence on the initial time. Preprint v2, 30 July 2025.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Enhanced dissipation, hypoellipticity, and anomalous small noise inviscid limits in shear flows
records.journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 224, 1161–1204
records.topic: smooth shear flows; hypocoercivity; partial diffusion
records.annotation: Foundational quantitative passive-scalar semigroup estimates for smooth finite-order critical shears on the torus and in a no-flux bounded channel, with full or transverse diffusion. Develops localized spectral-gap and hypocoercive energies, plus hypoellipticity. Nonzero streamwise modes are essential; some decay bounds have logarithmic losses removed by later methods. Boundary cases should use later sharp results rather than transferring the periodic statement unchanged.
records.verification_level: primary-source bibliographic metadata and abstract; selected theorem qualifications checked

records.title: Stable mixing estimates in the infinite Péclet number limit
records.topic: monotone shears; mixing and enhanced dissipation; commuting vector fields
records.annotation: Combines sharp monotone-shear L2 dissipation at rate proportional to ν^(1/3) with inviscid t^(−1) decay in a negative Sobolev norm, uniformly as ν tends to zero. Uses hypocoercivity and a vector field commuting with transport. Useful for explaining that mixing and enhanced dissipation are different estimates that can coexist in one bound.

records.title: A stochastic approach to enhanced diffusion
records.journal: Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, Classe di Scienze 22, 811–834
records.topic: sharpness; stochastic trajectories; shear and circular flows
records.annotation: Constructs scalar data saturating known enhanced-diffusion scales for Hölder shears, Lipschitz shears with critical points, and regular circular flows. Uses a probabilistic representation of scalar dissipation. Working reference for proving optimality, rather than merely repeating an upper decay bound.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation and Hörmander's hypoellipticity
records.topic: smooth shears; sharp boundary estimates; Hörmander commutators
records.annotation: Passive scalar on a periodic strip with periodic, Dirichlet, or Neumann transverse boundary conditions. Derives sharp finite-order shear dissipation scales from hypoelliptic/subelliptic estimates, including sharp monotone-channel behavior. Good modern complement to Bedrossian–Coti Zelati. Write the order-of-vanishing convention explicitly when quoting exponents: the arXiv abstract contains an apparent N versus N−1 inconsistency, so use theorem definitions in the full text.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation and Taylor dispersion in higher-dimensional parallel shear flows
records.journal: Journal of the London Mathematical Society 108(4), 1358–1392
records.topic: parallel shears; higher dimensions; Taylor dispersion; method comparison
records.annotation: Passive scalar in an infinite cylinder with bounded cross section. Proves optimal frequency-dependent decay under specified nondegeneracy conditions, covering enhanced dissipation when ν is much smaller than |k| and Taylor dispersion when |k| is much smaller than ν. Presents both resolvent/Gearhart–Prüss and direct hypocoercivity proofs. Excellent reference for a synthesis chapter, but the low-frequency whole-cylinder behavior must not be described as a single uniform exponential decay rate.

records.title: Analysis of enhanced diffusion in Taylor dispersion via a model problem
records.journal: Hamiltonian Partial Differential Equations and Applications, Fields Institute Communications 75, pp. 31–71
records.topic: Taylor dispersion; pedagogical model; center manifolds
records.annotation: A simplified tracer model for shear in an infinite channel. Uses Fourier and center-manifold methods to split exponential high-mode decay from algebraic low-mode behavior governed by an effective diffusion coefficient proportional to 1/ν. A useful elementary example preceding the full PDE treatment; do not conflate long-wave Taylor dispersion with nonzero-mode enhanced dissipation on a periodic channel.

records.title: Rigorous justification of Taylor dispersion via center manifolds and hypocoercivity
records.journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 235, 1105–1149
records.topic: Taylor dispersion; center manifolds; spectral decomposition; hypocoercivity
records.annotation: Rigorous passive-tracer PDE justification of Taylor dispersion. Decomposes the scalar into an approximate low-mode solution governed by a finite-dimensional center manifold and a faster-decaying remainder; uses spectral analysis and hypocoercivity at intermediate Fourier modes. Published online in 2019, with journal-volume year 2020.

records.title: Separation of time-scales in drift-diffusion equations on R²
records.journal: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 142, 58–75
records.topic: whole-plane circular flows; weighted hypocoercivity; axisymmetrization
records.annotation: Passive scalar stirred by radially symmetric incompressible flows in R². Obtains rapid equilibration along streamlines on a scale preceding ordinary diffusion; power-law scales depend on behavior near the origin. The semigroup estimate uses an appropriate weighted L2-based space. Do not present as full scalar homogenization in the whole plane.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation by circularly symmetric and parallel pipe flows
records.topic: circular flows; pipe flows; hyperdiffusion; resolvent
records.annotation: Uses m-accretive resolvent estimates to quantify enhanced decay for appropriately projected scalars under circular/cylindrical advection in two/three dimensions, allowing diffusion and hyperdiffusion. Extends Coti Zelati–Dolce in these geometries. The projection and nondegeneracy assumptions matter; do not claim enhanced decay for invariant components of arbitrary data.

records.title: Quantifying the dissipation enhancement of cellular flows
records.topic: cellular flows; coupling; dissipation and mixing time
records.annotation: Quantifies dissipation enhancement for a family of cellular flows in terms of flow amplitude, cell size and diffusivity, using probabilistic coupling and a comparison between dissipation and stochastic mixing times. Gives distinct regimes governed by one-cell exit and effective diffusivity. Keep the changing-cell-scale family separate from a fixed cellular Hamiltonian's small-diffusivity asymptotics.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation for two-dimensional Hamiltonian flows
records.journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 248, Article 84
records.topic: autonomous Hamiltonian flows; obstructions and sharpness; action-angle coordinates
records.annotation: Autonomous Hamiltonians in C1∩W2,p on compact two-dimensional manifolds. Derives upper bounds on possible dissipation rates through orbit-period behavior: at most O(ν^(1/3)) generally, with stronger obstructions near nondegenerate elliptic points, including an O(ν^(1/2)) bound for the standard cellular flow. Contains additional bounds for that example. This paper provides rate obstructions as well as constructive estimates; do not reverse upper bounds on a rate into upper bounds on a dissipation time.

records.title: Diffusion enhancement and Taylor dispersion for rotationally symmetric flows in discs and pipes
records.journal: Journal of Mathematical Fluid Mechanics 26, Article 12
records.topic: radial flows; circular flows; pipes; Taylor dispersion
records.annotation: Short passive-scalar treatment identifying velocity conditions for enhanced dissipation and Taylor dispersion in infinite three-dimensional pipes, with circular-flow decay on discs as a byproduct. Strong bridge between the radial example and the parallel-shear/Taylor-dispersion chapter. Journal publication date is 2024 despite a 2023 DOI suffix and some author-page shorthand.

records.title: Dissipation enhancing properties for a class of Hamiltonian flows with closed streamlines
records.journal: Communications in Partial Differential Equations 50 (2025), no. 3, 301-352
records.topic: Hamiltonian flows; closed streamlines; streamline averaging
records.annotation: For autonomous two-dimensional Hamiltonian velocities with nested closed streamlines and an elliptic point, proves fast approach to a streamline average up to a geometric correction for a specified class including perturbed radial flows. records.topic: Time-dependent shear flows; slowly moving critical points

records.title: Pseudo-Gevrey smoothing for the passive scalar equations near Couette
records.topic: Near-Couette passive scalars; boundary regularity
records.annotation: Studies the linear passive scalar and Poisson equations in a periodic finite channel for time-varying shears close to Couette. Establishes spatially varying pseudo-Gevrey regularity with adapted derivatives, homogeneous Dirichlet conditions and data supported away from the walls. Relevant advanced technical reference; its nonlinear Navier-Stokes companion is a separate paper. records.title: Mixing and enhanced dissipation in a time-translating shear flow
records.topic: Time-dependent shear flows; moving critical points
records.annotation: Studies the smooth prescribed translating sine shear on T^2, with streamwise-mean-free data. For c=c0*nu^ell, ell in (1/3,3/4), Theorem 2 gives modal squared-L2 decay exponent proportional to nu^p, p=(1+2*ell)/5, with a polynomial nu-dependent prefactor; inferring a uniform halving time introduces a logarithmic loss. The endpoints are limiting comparisons, not included parameter values. For large c, heat-equation approximation holds on fixed time intervals for H^2 data, not as a uniform-in-time no-enhancement theorem. Preprint v1, 15 March 2026.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation via time-modulated velocity fields
records.topic: Time-modulated shear flows; hypocoercivity
records.annotation: For passive scalar advection diffusion with velocity xi(t) times a shear, proves quantitative decay estimates depending on the modulation. Certain growing modulations produce faster decay than autonomous shears; switched-on/off examples retain comparable rates. Uses time-dependent weights in a hypocoercivity functional. Publisher gives volume year 2026 and online date 15 July 2025; the first arXiv title was Enhanced Dissipation via Time-Dependent Velocity Fields: Acceleration and Intermittency.

records.title: Localized Enhanced Dissipation: A Hypocoercivity Approach
records.topic: Shear flows; localized hypocoercivity
records.annotation: For stationary shear passive scalars on T^2 or T x R with finitely many nondegenerate critical points, Theorem 1.1 controls a space-time weighted L2 norm of a rescaled nonzero Fourier mode using hypocoercivity. The global rate remains nu^(1/2); the weight resolves faster decay away from critical layers, but saturates after time nu^(-1/2), so it does not assert a permanent global nu^(1/3) rate away from critical points. Preprint v1 submitted 15 March 2026; the rendered manuscript internally bears the date 24 August 2026.

records.title: Optimal enhanced dissipation and mixing for a time-periodic, Lipschitz velocity field on T2
records.topic: deterministic alternating shears; optimal logarithmic dissipation time
records.annotation: Constructs a fixed time-periodic Lipschitz incompressible velocity alternating between two piecewise-linear shears on T2. Proves exponential inviscid mixing and dissipation time of order |log nu|, optimal in the uniformly Lipschitz class. This is a deterministic positive-diffusivity result, stronger in scope than a construction mixing only one chosen initial scalar.

records.title: Mixing and diffusion for rough shear flows
records.journal: Ars Inveniendi Analytica, Paper No. 2, 21 pp.
records.topic: Hölder shears; limits of mixing heuristics
records.annotation: Studies passive scalars driven by C^α stationary shears. Shows roughness can speed dissipation substantially without a corresponding uniform acceleration of inviscid mixing beyond smooth monotone-shear behavior. Useful counterexample to treating a mixing-rate heuristic as a universal equivalence.

records.title: Enhanced dissipation, hypoellipticity for passive scalar equations with fractional dissipation
records.topic: fractional dissipation; shear critical points; resolvent; hypoellipticity
records.annotation: Proves enhanced-dissipation and hypoelliptic estimates for passive scalars under steady periodic shear advection with finite-order critical points and fractional dissipation, including a cross-stream-only diffusion model. The proved fractional-power range is gamma in (1/2,2]; bounds contain logarithmic losses in part of that range. At gamma=1 the estimates recover the sharp classical shear rate. Appropriate for an extension chapter; do not state a theorem for every positive fractional power or omit its profile hypotheses.

records.title: Mixing for generic rough shear flows
records.topic: generic rough shears; prevalence; Besov regularity; mixing and dissipation
records.annotation: Studies passive-scalar mixing and enhanced dissipation for generic rough shear profiles, where generic means prevalence rather than an assertion about every rough profile. Regularity is measured in Besov–Nikolskii B-alpha_(1,infinity), alpha in (0,1). Derives upper/lower bounds identifying the dissipation-rate power nu^(alpha/(alpha+2)) and the corresponding inviscid mixing scale, using rho-irregularity. Complements explicit rough-shear constructions; retain the genericity and function-space qualifications when presenting the results.

records.topic: higher-dimensional shears; fractional/high-order/variable diffusion

records.annotation: Studies passive scalar advection diffusion on the two-dimensional torus for very rough horizontal shears in negative Besov spaces. records.annotation: Passive scalar on T^d with random smooth velocities, including suitably forced 2D stochastic Navier–Stokes flows. Proves almost-sure exponential H−1 mixing uniformly in scalar diffusivity and L2 enhanced dissipation after a logarithmic-in-diffusivity waiting time. records.topic: random dynamical systems; smooth universal exponential mixers
records.annotation: Develops a dynamical/Harris-theorem framework for smooth time-uniformly bounded universal exponential mixing, applied to randomized alternating periodic shears. records.topic: Random alternating shears; Harris methods

records.topic: Transport noise; qualitative criterion; stochastic shears
records.annotation: Develops a stochastic RAGE theorem for the two-point motion of noisy transport and a necessary and sufficient criterion for dissipation enhancement of the corresponding diffusive equation. records.topic: Random mixing flows; spherical geometry
records.annotation: Constructs smooth incompressible prescribed velocities on the unit sphere by alternating two Rossby-Haurwitz flows with random amplitudes. records.title: Zufällige Bewegungen (Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung)
records.topic: history; Kolmogorov equation; Brownian motion; Fokker–Planck equation; explicit fundamental solution
records.annotation: Two-page note (received 9 September 1933) that applies Kolmogorov's theory of continuous random processes to random motions in which the coordinates and also their time derivatives change continuously. The transition density solves a Fokker–Planck equation with second derivatives only in the velocities (eq. (9)); for one degree of freedom and constant coefficients (eq. (10), with no force) it is the equation of the Couette flow without the diffusion along the streamlines, the velocity in the role of y. He writes its fundamental solution (eq. (11)) and reads off that the velocity changes by an amount of order (Δt)^(1/2) while the position deviates from the free motion by an amount of order (Δt)^(3/2) (eq. (12)). Nothing on smoothness or hypoellipticity: that reading is Hörmander's (1967). Cited on the page Couette flow for the history of the model. Formula (11) as printed has misprints in the constants (k³ where k should be, prefactor 2√3/(πk²(t'−t)²) instead of √3/(2πk(t'−t)²)): checked symbolically on 11 November 2026; use the corrected formula. The author's name is printed A. Kolmogoroff; cited in the text as Kolmogorov (1934). Title in Crossref without the umlaut.
records.verification_level: the paper read (PDF from JSTOR supplied by M. Dolce); bibliographic metadata from the Crossref record of the DOI
